LESSON: READING 9.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMILES AND METAPHORS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors, part of Strand 9 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What makes short stories interesting? 2. Why should short stories be read? 3. How can one write a short story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. list the similes and metaphors in a given short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use similes and metaphors in their own sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the importance of similes and metaphors in communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. list the similes and metaphors in a given short story,

   Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use similes and metaphors in their own sentences,

   Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story,

   Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. acknowledge the importance of similes and metaphors in communication.

   Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online and offline for meanings of simile and metaphor,

2. read a given short story and identify the similes and metaphors present,

3. discuss the meanings of the similes and metaphors identified,

4. discuss the relevance of the similes and metaphors in the short story,

5. list the similes and metaphors they know,

6. construct sentences using the similes and metaphors in the context of African heroes and heroines. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online and offline for meanings of simile and metaphor,
2. read a given short story and identify the similes and metaphors present,
3. discuss the meanings of the similes and metaphors identified,
4. discuss the relevance of the similes and metaphors in the short story,
5. list the similes and metaphors they know,
6. construct sentences using the similes and metaphors in the context of African heroes and heroines. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: National and cultural identity is enhanced as the learner uses metaphors and similes in the context of African

heroes:

• Collaboration: Team work is enhanced as the learner respects the opinion of others while contributing to group discussions

on similes and metaphors.

Values:
Respect: Discussion on heroes and heroines inculcates respect for the citizens of the different countries.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship education (Patriotism): Constructing sentences in the context of African heroes and heroines makes the learner

identify with Africa.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The concept of metaphors and similes is relevant to the learning of stylistic devices in Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. list the similes and metaphors in a given short story,
2. use similes and metaphors in their own sentences,
3. explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story,
4. acknowledge the importance of similes and metaphors in communication.

Remember the key question: What makes short stories interesting? 2. Why should short stories be read? 3. How can one write a short story?
